module.title: 4 · Vector error correction
module.summary: Combine short-run changes with adjustment toward long-run equilibrium.

stages.title: Vector error correction: research guide
stages.html:
Vector error correction

Combine short-run changes with adjustment toward long-run equilibrium.

The cointegrating vector defines disequilibrium; adjustment coefficients describe which variables respond to that gap.

Workflow. Combine long-run equilibrium errors with short-run changes.

Diagnostic: Inspect adjustment coefficients, cointegrating vectors, and stability. The main failure to avoid is calling every adjustment coefficient a causal response.

stages.title: Vector error correction intuition lab
stages.note: Set the adjustment speed at which y1 error-corrects to the long-run relation, then let statsmodels VECM recover the loading and cointegrating vector — larger speed means the equilibrium error snaps back faster.
stages.template:
import numpy as np
from statsmodels.tsa.vector_ar.vecm import VECM
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
n = 250; alpha = {{alpha}}; beta = {{beta}}
y1 = np.zeros(n); y2 = np.zeros(n)
for t in range(1, n):
    ec = y1[t-1] - beta*y2[t-1]                      # disequilibrium gap
    y2[t] = y2[t-1] + rng.normal(0, 1)               # random-walk driver
    y1[t] = y1[t-1] - alpha*ec + rng.normal(0, 1)    # error-correction pull
data = np.column_stack([y1, y2])
m = VECM(data, k_ar_diff=0, coint_rank=1, deterministic='n').fit()
a_hat = m.alpha.ravel()[0]
bv = m.beta.ravel(); slope_hat = -(bv[1]/bv[0])       # normalized slope
ec_series = y1 - beta*y2
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.2, 3.4))
ax[0].plot(y1, color='#da9100', label='y1'); ax[0].plot(y2, color='#4f8fba', label='y2')
ax[0].legend(fontsize=8); ax[0].set_title('Levels track a common path')
ax[1].plot(ec_series, color='#c0392b'); ax[1].axhline(0, color='#888', lw=0.8)
ax[1].set_title('Equilibrium error (mean-reverts when alpha>0)')
plt.tight_layout()
print(f'true alpha={alpha:.2f}  estimated loading={a_hat:.3f} (|loading| grows with alpha)')
print(f'true beta={beta:.2f}  estimated cointegrating slope={slope_hat:.2f}')

stages.title: Vector error correction: worked Python model
stages.note: Run the reproducible example, then change one assumption and compare the output.
stages.code:
prior_mean, prior_var = 1.2, 0.9
measurement, measurement_var = 2.0, 0.4
gain = prior_var / (prior_var + measurement_var)
posterior_mean = prior_mean + gain*(measurement-prior_mean)
posterior_var = (1-gain)*prior_var
print(f"Kalman gain: {gain:.3f}")
print(f"Posterior state: {posterior_mean:.3f}")
print(f"Posterior variance: {posterior_var:.3f}")

expected_gain = prior_var/(prior_var+measurement_var)
expected_mean = prior_mean+expected_gain*(measurement-prior_mean)
assert abs(gain-expected_gain) < 1e-10
assert abs(posterior_mean-expected_mean) < 1e-10
print("grader: Kalman update is correct")
hints: Gain is prior variance divided by total prior-plus-measurement variance.
Update the prior by gain times the measurement innovation.

steps.prompt: What is the best next action?
choices: Update a latent-state estimate by balancing prior and measurement uncertainty.
Increase decimal precision and report immediately.
Drop observations until the preferred coefficient appears.
steps.explain: The defensible workflow is to update a latent-state estimate by balancing prior and measurement uncertainty.

a state estimate that ignores signal-to-noise information
Whether every coefficient has the same sign.
